body.en:
Question B-003-016-008.

Why the correct answer is right: A capacity rating is tied to specified discharge conditions. Drawing more current than that rating condition makes the battery run down faster than the label alone suggests.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "One or more cells may become short-circuited": Internal cell shorts are fault conditions, not the normal effect of simply drawing more than the specified capacity-test current.
- sourceIndex 2: "The battery will accept the subsequent charge in a shorter time": Heavy discharge does not guarantee faster safe charging; the charger and chemistry set the allowed charge rate.
- sourceIndex 3: "The voltage delivered will be higher": Higher load current normally increases voltage sag because of internal resistance, so the delivered voltage tends to be lower, not higher.
